key_idea: Build the key-position maps for the left hand shifted right and right hand shifted left (preserving the shift layer), then test the candidate and its case-swapped version against identity, LS, RS, one insertion and one deletion.
sketch: Model the QWERTY rows in unshifted and shifted layers; the left hand covers `12345/qwert/asdfg/zxcvb and the rest is the right hand. LS maps each left key to the key on its right in the same layer, RS maps each right key to the key on its left. For each test string t and for t with letter case toggled (CL), accept if it equals p, LS(p), RS(p), or differs from p by exactly one inserted or one deleted character. At most one of LS/RS/EC/MC may be combined with CL, so LS+RS or LS+MC must be rejected. Pitfalls: the keyboard figure is missing from the scraped text so the hand split (e.g. the 6 key) and the backslash position are assumed from the standard layout; read lines whole since punctuation is arbitrary.
